original_question: Suppose there exists a counterexample to the hf/hf problem, namely an hf/hf countable Borel equivalence relation that is not hyperfinite. Would it then follow that the set of all hyperfinite equivalence relations is Σ1_2-complete?
target_in_paper: Section 10 (Su Gao), Problem 39, as set up by Problem 37 (the hf/hf problem), Theorem 38, and the preceding analogy with Theorem 36.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the hypothesis is the existence of a counterexample to the hf/hf problem, correctly interprets this as an hf/hf countable Borel equivalence relation that is not hyperfinite, and correctly states that the conclusion being asked about is Σ^1_2-completeness of the class of hyperfinite equivalence relations.
missing_details: The ambient objects are countable Borel equivalence relations, i.e. countable Borel equivalence relations on a standard Borel space X.
The paper’s shorthand “hf/hf” means “hyperfinite-over-hyperfinite,” and this should be defined explicitly.
The hf/hf hypothesis is: there exists a Borel partial order ≤ on X such that if x ≤ y, then x E y.

The classwise order condition is also part of the definition: for each x, the order type of ≤ restricted to [x]_E is a suborder of Z^2 (equivalently, a Borel Z^2-ordering in the nearby Gao–Xiao formulation).
The conclusion concerns the class of hyperfinite countable Borel equivalence relations, not arbitrary equivalence relations.
The phrase “Σ^1_2-complete” implicitly refers to the usual descriptive-set-theoretic coding of countable Borel equivalence relations; the open-problem paper leaves this coding implicit.
The nearby context matters: Problem 39 is explicitly posed as the hf/hf analogue of Theorem 36 about the union problem.
Theorem 38 supplies an explicit equivalent reformulation of the hf/hf counterexample hypothesis via failure of a self-compatible Borel Z^2-ordering.
refined_question: Assume there exists a countable Borel equivalence relation E on a standard Borel space X that is hyperfinite-over-hyperfinite (hf/hf), meaning that E admits a Borel partial order ≤ on X such that (i) x ≤ y implies x E y, and (ii) for each x in X, the ordered class ([x]_E, ≤↾[x]_E) has order type embeddable into the lexicographically ordered Z×Z; and assume moreover that E is not hyperfinite. Does it follow that, in the usual coding of countable Borel equivalence relations, the class of hyperfinite countable Borel equivalence relations is Σ^1_2-complete?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Theorem 38: if there exists an hf/hf countable Borel equivalence relation E that does not admit a self-compatible Borel Z^2-ordering, must the class of hyperfinite countable Borel equivalence relations be Σ^1_2-complete?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 39 in Section 10. The paper first recalls the union problem and the Frisch–Shinko–Vidnyánszky complexity theorem (Problem 35 and Theorem 36), then defines hf/hf just before Problem 37, states the hf/hf problem in Problem 37, and immediately gives Theorem 38 as an equivalent characterization of hyperfiniteness for hf/hf relations. Problem 39 is then posed explicitly as the hf/hf analogue of Theorem 36. So the main sharpening needed is only to make the hf/hf definition and the ambient descriptive-set-theoretic coding implicit in “Σ^1_2-complete” explicit, while keeping the scope exactly at the level of Problem 39.
